title: First 10 Seconds — Claim Checklist & Hero Variants
content:
Context:
This doc is a working checklist for copy that must land in the visitor's first 10 seconds on the homepage or product landing. Goal: rapid comprehension of what Redwood does and why engineers care — measured by click-throughs to quickstart, signup conversion for evaluation credits, and product-led activation (first API call).

Problem framing (why 10s matters):
- Behavioral baseline: users form an initial impression in <10s; if value isn’t explicit, they bounce.
- Engineers scan for three things: what it does, how it helps my job, how to try it quickly.
- Site currently emphasizes high-level benefits (performance, reliability) but lacks a crisp hook mapping to engineer actions (try, benchmark, integrate).

Primary claim objectives (ranked):
1) Precise outcome: predictable inference performance (latency + cost)
2) Clear action: integrate or benchmark in <10 minutes
3) Differentiator: same API and tooling across hosted/dedicated/private
4) Safety/enterprise reassurance: SLA/PKI/KMS mention in secondary area

User-facing constraint: 12 words max for primary hero line; 6–12 words for subhead. Microtests should be short enough to land on mobile small screens.

Hero copy variants (compact, aim to test meaningfully different mental models):
Variant A — "Control latency. Cut cost. Ship reliable LLM features."
Subhead: "One API. Hosted, reserved, or private — same code, predictable economics. Start with a free API key."
CTA1: "Run a sample in 60s" | CTA2: "Compare performance"

Variant B — "Make LLM inference predictable — from dev to production."
Subhead: "Autoscaling, KV caching, and model fallbacks tuned for real apps. Pin versions, not surprise bills."
CTA1: "Quickstart guide" | CTA2: "See benchmarks"

Variant C — "Ship LLM features without building inference infra."
Subhead: "Developer-first runtime, enterprise controls, and cost-lean defaults. Try hosted or bring your own GPU."
CTA1: "Start free" | CTA2: "Dedicated plans"

Variant D (emotion-first) — "Confidence for your LLM stack — predictable, observable, and resilient."
Subhead: "From dev tests to SLA-backed deployments: a single interface for all inference modes."
CTA1: "Run our quick demo"

Microcopy experiments (below hero):
- Try small bullet proofs: "< 50ms median for short prompts*" / "Batch-aware pricing" / "Model pinning & rollouts"
- Quick checklist link: "Can I drop this into prod? (Yes/No)" — leads to a 4-step checklist page with real config examples.

Proof point panel ideas (short lines for first fold):
- Real customers: "X enterprise reduced inference cost by 38% when moving to Redwood Dedicated (anon case)."
- Speed claim: "Median latency 30–70ms on 8k context (redwood-blue profile)."
- Ops claim: "Rollouts, canary, automatic fallback — built-in."
(Notes: we must gate precise numbers behind linked benchmark page and include asterisks).

Competitor contrast sketches (to include beneath proof panel as a short bullets cluster):
- Big cloud endpoints: easy to deploy, but variable tail latency and limited model-level batching controls.
- Model-hosting APIs: good for access, not for unit-economics at scale or private deployments.
- Self-hosted runtimes: maximum control but high ops cost and long time-to-prod.

Suggested short contrast copy: "More predictable than endpoints. Less ops than self-hosting." (Test this vs. stronger phrasing: "Better unit economics than hosted endpoints, less work than self-hosting.")

Measurement plan / metrics to attach to variations:
- Primary: 7-day conversion (visitor -> signup -> first API call)
- Secondary: time on quickstart, bounce rate on first fold, click rate on "See benchmarks"
- Qualitative: session recordings for visitors who bounce in <8s (why?)

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Cohort 1: Variant A vs. B on mobile (50/50) 2wks
- Cohort 2: Variant C vs. D on desktop (50/50) 2wks
- Cohort 3: A + proof panel vs. A + checklist link (mobile)

Content hygiene & legal notes:
- Any numeric claim pulled into hero must link to a benchmark page and include test conditions (model, prompt length, hardware profile).
- Avoid direct named comparisons to identified competitors — use generic contrasts.
- All customer logos/proof require signed permission.

Open questions / decisions for product: (action owners tagged)
- Do we want a live tiny demo in the hero (sample API call streaming) or static code block? [Product/Engineering: Priya K to advise on infra cost]
- Should we surface "hosted | dedicated | private" as a pill selector in hero to personalize messaging? [Design + Analytics: testability needed]
- Which benchmark profiles become the default proof? (short vs. long prompts) [Applied ML: Ethan M]

Quick implementation checklist for a launch candidate (MVP hero):
1) Pick top hero variant (marketing + product vote) — target: Variant A or B.
2) Wire CTA to a pre-baked quickstart with API key issuance and a one-click sample call.
3) Add 3-line proof panel with links to benchmark page with test configs.
4) A/B test infrastructure: set up analytics funnels, session recordings, and attribution for experiments.
5) Legal review of any numerical claims.

Notes to reviewers:
- Keep iterations short — run 2-week rounds and kill or promote quickly.
- This doc should be the single source for copy that experiments with low-friction call-to-actions.

Appendix: short alternate micro-phrases to reuse across pages (snappy):
- "Pin models. Predict cost. Ship fast."
- "Same API, three deployment shapes."
- "Fall back automatically when capacity shifts."
- "Turn benchmarks into shipped features."

End of doc — comments welcome inline.
